posts.title: A Mother’s Tiara, a Queen’s Emeralds: Royal & Noble Jewels at Sotheby’s Geneva, Part II
posts.description: A tiara made to flatter the Second Empire became a wedding gift for the Orléans pretender’s bride; her daughter’s emeralds followed a Portuguese queen into exile. posts.title: The Hand That Sets the Stone: The Bulgari Pink and the Great Houses at Christie’s Geneva
posts.description: Set by Bulgari in 1950s Rome and kept in private hands for more than seventy years, a 24-carat pink diamond reaches auction for the first time, beside a collection built around the great jewellery houses. posts.title: A Queen’s Copy, an Empress’s Gift: Provenance and the 19th Century at Phillips Geneva
posts.description: In 1928 Queen Mary commissioned a copy of Victoria's Jubilee necklace. Nearly a century later, it returns to auction in Geneva alongside a gem-set cross from Rudolf Nureyev's collection.
